title: C++ & Raylib
author: DatabaseConstant7870
selftext: I know I’m not the only one trying to get away from web based games and make games that are executable and use the players gpu and cpu instead of web computing power. I recently started building a game I built out in three.js and I’m finding it to much more tedious. With three.js games I could typically use free gpt to create a master prompt to feed cursor. That does not seem to work with c++ and raylib, I’m also using ninja and llvm. Anyone else have experience they’d like to share.

comments.author: Melodic-Chemistry127
comments.body: Why do you plunge from Javascript all the way down to C++ and raylib? Try Godot C# instead. LLMs are pretty good at it.

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: Well as many have noticed ai does real well with three.js and I’ve used mcps and everything with unity and I’ve done some cool stuff but I feel like I’m trapped to what the engine can do and there’s stuff I can get around without a game engine’s limitations. I think I might just try to recreate a voxel game system first and get an understanding of what my workflow needs to be

replies.author: Melodic-Chemistry127
replies.body: The consensus in software engineering circles is, that AIs are not that great with C/C++. You're going to hit one brick wall after another. I guarantee you, that whatever you can get done with raw C++ and raylib can be done with an engine. You just need to figure out how.

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: Yeah after messing with it for like 3 hours last night it kinda felt like I was vibecoding back in 2013 before vibecoding meant using AI, I got a cool decent little bar scene and first person mechanics fast and nodes that were obviously for placeholders for asset models. I replaced them but it took the ai a min to figure out what it needed to do to get the mesh built correctly in the game, it worked from there I worked in a system for moving the assets around the room it worked but needed tweaking, from there I needed to hit the hay cuz it was really just a late night adventure for a few hours

comments.author: FutureLynx_
comments.body: Prefer JS because C++ you need to compile. Why do you want to move to C++? I want to move to JS from C++ and Unreal...

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: Honestly just to do something different. I feel like everyone uses a game engine or js, i don’t see any videos of people trying c++ with no game engine, but i see a lot of three.js web browser games. I built out an idea with three js and it’s cool but it’s a web browser game and yes i guess i could use tauri to make it an executable and keep working on it but there’s something about building it a way no one else is currently.

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body:
I specialized in Unreal and C++. My advice is to go for Unreal only if you intend to become a professional or work in the industry. Also +1 if most of your game ideas are 3D.

In any other scenario, you are much better off going for Godot. It takes 10x more time to make a game in Unreal than in Godot, except for FPS.

Im working with Unreal, and im trying to find an alternative. And Godot is much better in terms of workflow, but since half of my game ideas are simple 2D games, I will use Phaser or just plain JS. These are fast and work great with AI.
